# R laboratories
## Code is evidence only when the epidemiological question and assumptions are visible.
<span class="lipps-chip">8 labs</span> <span class="lipps-chip">Synthetic teaching data</span> <span class="lipps-chip">Reproducible</span>
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Laboratory sequence
1. [Disease frequency and standardisation](lab-01-standardisation.qmd)
2. [Crude and adjusted effects](lab-02-effects.qmd)
3. [Survey prevalence and weights](lab-03-survey.qmd)
4. [Case-control analysis](lab-04-case-control.qmd)
5. [Survival analysis](lab-05-survival.qmd)
6. [Trials and quasi-experiments](lab-06-trials-quasi.qmd)
7. [Diagnostic accuracy](lab-07-diagnostics.qmd)
8. [Surveillance and outbreak signals](lab-08-surveillance.qmd)

All datasets are fictional and generated for teaching. They are deliberately small enough to run on ordinary laptops. The displayed R code is non-executable in Quarto so the public site does not require an R runtime during deployment.
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Submission standard
A laboratory submission should include the question, estimand, reproducible code, one diagnostic/assumption check, a concise results paragraph and a **What could fool us?** note. A technically correct model without a defensible epidemiological interpretation is incomplete.
:::
